findings.title: Sender validation is bypassed when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the Integration.DoesNotExist branch immediately returns pipeline.next_step(), while the github_authenticated_user versus integration.metadata["sender"] comparison at lines 500-505 only runs when an Integration already exists without an OrganizationIntegration. A newly installed GitHub App therefore completes without any sender check if the installation webhook has not yet created the Integration row (a normal race, since GitHub sends the webhook and the user redirect independently) or if the webhook was missed/delayed. An attacker who installed the app can have a different Sentry user claim that installation_id during that window, defeating the validation this PR is intended to add; the check needs to fail closed or obtain the installer identity from a source available at build_integration/finish time rather than relying solely on a pre-existing row.

findings.title: Sender check raises KeyError for integrations created without sender metadata
findings.body: The check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. Integrations created through the normal pipeline only get metadata["sender"] when state happens to contain a sender (the updated test's basic flow asserts metadata with no sender key), and integrations created before sender tracking existed likewise lack it. When such an Integration exists but its OrganizationIntegration has been removed, this line raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of either proceeding or showing the integration-failed page, breaking reinstallation/moving of those integrations. The lookup should use a safe .get() chain and define the behavior when sender is absent.

findings.title: Token-exchange network errors escape the graceful error handling
findings.body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen() before the try block; only safe_urlread()/decoding/parsing is wrapped. If GitHub's access-token endpoint is unreachable, resets the connection, or safe_urlopen rejects/errors on the request, the exception propagates as an unhandled 500 instead of rendering the github-integration-failed page that the PR promises for a failed code exchange. The safe_urlopen call (and the unguarded get_user_info call that follows) should be covered by the same failure path that handles a missing access_token.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The rewritten test supplies state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which does not match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-request page before build_integration/get_installation_info is ever reached. The test therefore passes even if the GitHub 404 handling ('The GitHub installation could not be found.') is broken or removed, and it silently drops the previous coverage/assertion for that message. The test should drive the flow with the correct pipeline state and an installation_id step so the mocked 404 from /app/installations/{id} is what produces the failure.
